summary: A small white wooden tower on Baie Verte, built in 1890 as the Chignecto Ship Railway was being laid out; dark since 2013 and now a designated Heritage Lighthouse.

events.note: Light exhibited on opening of navigation, spring 1890

evidence.supports: fixed white light, 60 ft, 13 miles, tower 36 ft white, red lantern
evidence.quote: It will be a fixed white light, elevated 60 feet above H.W.

evidence.supports: contract $894, J. Harvey Brownell first keeper 12 April 1890
evidence.quote: The tower was built at a cost of $894 under contract to J. Harvey Brownell

evidence.supports: resigned after thirteen months; Alfred Brownell relative
evidence.quote: After just thirteen months at the post

evidence.supports: Chignecto Ship Railway, Baring collapse 1890, light deactivated 2013
evidence.quote: The failure to finish the project certainly diminished the amount of marine traffic
In 2015, Cold Spring Head Lighthouse was designated a Heritage Lighthouse

evidence.supports: owner Coast Guard, grounds open, tower closed; directions
built in anticipation of increased traffic
evidence.quote: as it was built in anticipation of increased maritime traffic
classically inspired frieze, comprised of a series of ornate brackets below the lantern gallery

evidence.supports: very good example of early square-tapered wooden tower, craftsmanship
evidence.quote: The Tower is a very good example of a typical, early prototype of the square-tapered wooden tower.
Federal Heritage Building Review Office Informal Building Report 90-106

evidence.supports: Cold Spring Head Road off NS 366

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Record shows 1889 (structure) and 1890 (directory); the 1890 Nautical Magazine notice via Lighthousefriends says the light would show on opening of navigation in spring 1890, so 1890 is first lit.

notes_for_editor: Thin station; core facts rest on Lighthousefriends (secondary, quoting The Nautical Magazine Jan 1890 and the Department of Marine reports) and heritage statements. Keeper dates are Lighthousefriends' only; not independently verified. Department of Marine lightkeeper lists name a Willard Vanemburg (1909) and Fred P. Ackles (1914) but the OCR columns could not be tied to this station, so they were left out of the story. Report 90-106 year (1990) inferred from number only, so the story gives no year. Converted 60 ft to 18 m and 100 ft to 30 m; 13 miles left as the notice gave it.
